statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-8328: ftplib.ftpcp() passed the host address from the source server's PASV reply straight to the target server, so a malicious source server could point the target's data connection at an arbitrary host (SSRF); the CVE-2021-4189 fix had covered only FTP.makepasv(). Upstream tracked it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/87451 and fixed it on the 3.12 branch in https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/c88704431ea3248ca769384c13856330976fac1d, first released in CPython 3.12.14. See https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/ITF2BAPBQEPYK3LDMPRSY435JGNHYNDP/ and https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-8328. We read /usr/lib/python3.12/ftplib.py in every python-3.12 package published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 24 versions, 3.12.12-r0 to 3.12.16-r4, x86_64 and aarch64, each matching its repository index checksum; both architectures agree. Builds up to 3.12.13-r11 ship a file byte-identical to CPython v3.12.13's Lib/ftplib.py, which passes the PASV address through. 3.12.13-r12 carries the upstream change as a backport ahead of the 3.12.14 release: it and every later build ship a file byte-identical to CPython v3.12.14's Lib/ftplib.py, where ftpcp() uses the source connection's peer address unless trust_server_pasv_ipv4_address is set. In every build on both architectures, the compiled ftplib files in python-3.12-pycache-pyc0, -pyc1 and -pyc2 are checked-hash .pyc files whose source hash matches the ftplib.py of the same build. The range ends at 3.12.13-r12.
